Subject: Redwood private deployment — network & go‑live questions

Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. We're close to scheduling the migration window for our private deployment (VPC peering + on‑prem connector). Before we lock dates, can you confirm the minimum networking prerequisites and any gating items we must clear with our infra team?

Specific asks:
- Port and CIDR lists for egress/ingress (control plane, runtime, metrics)
- Whether SSH access or bastion is required for the on‑prem worker onboarding
- TLS / client cert expectations (mTLS?) for the connector
- Any required Service Accounts / IAM roles we should provision ahead of time

We also need a short runbook for our ops folks that lists prechecks and a quick rollback plan.

Can your team send a checklist and any templates we can use to validate our environment? Preferable to have this before EOD Wed so we can book an April 1 window.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment — network & go‑live questions

Hi Nathan —

Great questions. I've attached a focused runbook and a k8s deployment template that our Private team uses during onboarding.

High‑level answers inline:
- Ports/CIDRs: see attachment "network-ports-required.csv" (control plane, runtime, metrics). Control plane uses 443 outbound to redwood-managed endpoints; runtime requires inbound from your NAT to the dedicated IP range we'll provide.
- SSH: A bastion is recommended for initial worker bootstrap if you want interactive troubleshooting. It's not strictly required for automated installs if you run our agent with the provided installer.
- TLS: Connector uses mutual TLS. You'll generate a client cert (CN=<customer-org>) and we exchange CA info during provisioning.
- IAM: Create a service account with network admin (to create routes) and a k8s cluster role with permissions to create RBAC, CRDs, and deployments. Exact role spec is in the template.

Quick prechecks we'd like you to run (short checklist):
1) Confirm VPC CIDR doesn't overlap with the on‑prem ranges you plan to peer.
2) Ensure outbound NAT for control plane IPs (see CSV).
3) Verify kubelet + API server versions (we support 1.24+; see template comments).
4) Ensure at least one jump host for initial troubleshooting (if using bastion flow).

Attachments:
- redwood_vpc_prereqs_v1.xlsx (runbook + precheck table)
- k8s-deployment-template.yaml

Next steps: if you can send the network team the CSV we generate (attached by Dev in next message), we'll set up a short validation call and a test deploy in our staging connector.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Nathan — attaching the canonical port/CIDR export we hand to customers. Quick notes inline and a very small script to validate connectivity from your ops jump host.

Key ports (excerpt):
- 443 outbound to control.redwood-inference.com (TCP) — control plane API and auth
- 52345 inbound (TCP) — runtime agent callback (optional, only for on‑prem worker mode)
- 8125 UDP (metrics) — optional; can be routed to internal statsd

Validation script (bash):
- curl -v https://control.redwood-inference.com/health
- nc -vz <control_ip> 443

Attachment: network-ports-required.csv

If you prefer, we can run the connectivity checks from our staging connector during the validation call. Ping here with a 60‑minute window that works.

—Dev
